findings.problem: TokenWorkflow uses raw String for status and bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of enums or typestates. This allows illegal states such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=true with status="created". No invariant enforcement exists.
findings.failure_mode: Any combination of status string and boolean flags is constructible, so downstream code cannot trust these fields to represent a coherent token lifecycle. Bug detection requires manual invariant checks at every access site instead of compile-time guarantees.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum `TokenStatus { Created, Validated, Sent }` or equivalent. Replace `is_validated: bool` and `is_sent: bool` with a typestate enum or derive them from `TokenStatus`. Make `TokenWorkflow` fields private and provide a fallible constructor that validates invariants.

findings.problem: `id: String` is a raw primitive with no domain identity. A Token ID has parsing, format, and uniqueness rules that should be enforced at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: Any string can be used as a token ID, including empty strings, malformed strings, or strings from unrelated domains. This prevents the compiler from distinguishing Token IDs from arbitrary strings in function signatures.
findings.fix: Introduce `pub struct TokenId(String)` with a private inner field and a fallible constructor `TokenId::new(s: &str) -> Result<TokenId, ParseError>` that validates the ID format. Use `TokenId` in the struct instead of raw `String`.

findings.problem: `mark_sent` takes ownership of the struct and mutates it in-place, returning the mutated struct. This is an imperative pattern that should be a pure function accepting an immutable reference and returning a new state, or a constructor that validates the state transition.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can call `mark_sent` even when the token has not been validated, producing an invalid state transition (created -> sent without validation). No precondition checks exist.
findings.fix: Make `mark_sent` a pure function: `pub fn mark_sent(item: &TokenWorkflow) -> Result<TokenWorkflow, TransitionError>` that validates the pre-condition (e.g., status == Validated) before returning a new state with status=Sent and sent_at_epoch_ms set.

findings.problem: All fields of TokenWorkflow are `pub`, allowing external code to mutate any field directly without going through constructors or validators. This bypasses all invariant enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set `item.is_sent = false` after `mark_sent()` returns, or set `item.status = "deleted"` which has no enum variant, breaking all assumptions about token lifecycle.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (`id`, `status`, `sent_at_epoch_ms`). Provide factory constructors and immutable accessors. State transitions go through dedicated functions or methods.

findings.problem: `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` uses a raw primitive for a temporal domain value. No parsing or validation wrapper exists for timestamp values.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can store arbitrary u64 values (e.g., 0, MAX, future dates) that may cause incorrect time comparisons or overflow in downstream arithmetic.
findings.fix: Introduce `SentAt(Instant)` or `SentAt(u64)` with a newtype wrapper and documented invariants. Use `std::time::Instant` or `SystemTime` for real time, or validate u64 ranges at construction.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation behavior
no profiler data for TokenWorkflow size and layout
no allocation analysis for String copies in mark_sent (to_string() on line 10)
no second-ring test evidence for state transition invariants
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has no tests, no benchmarks, and no CI gates. The core domain model is fundamentally underspecified — all invariants are runtime-only with no type-level protection. The most dangerous gap is that `mark_sent` has zero pre-condition checking and can produce illegal state transitions.
